pages.text: Converts a number to a FLOAT.$(br2)You rarely need it. An INTEGER goes into a FLOAT variable, parameter or result by itself, $(1)/$() always gives a FLOAT, and the math functions and $(1)%f$() of FORMAT take INTEGERs too.

Use it when a calculation with INTEGERs gets too big: $(1)+$(), $(1)*$() and $(1)^$() of two INTEGERs raise NUMERIC_OVERFLOW above 9223372036854775807, with a FLOAT they don't. Or when a text should show a FLOAT: $(1)⊕$() writes the INTEGER 8 as $(1)8$() and the FLOAT as $(1)8.0$().
$(li)$(1)value$() INTEGER|FLOAT: the number$(li)result $(1)result$() FLOAT: the same number as FLOAT
$(1)CALL c0de/math/TO_FLOAT$(br)  PARAMETER value count ;$(br)  RESULT result amount$()
